report.incidentSummary: On 2026-10-14 around 09:10 IST (03:40 UTC), users reported that their mutual fund holdings and P&L displayed stale values from the previous day, while stock valuations functioned normally without application errors. Investigation revealed that the scheduled nightly mutual fund NAV import job failed overnight at 23:32 IST (18:02 UTC on 2026-10-13) within market-data-service due to an unhandled parse error ('N.A.' string instead of a numerical NAV) on line 8982 of AMFI's NAVAll.txt file. The import aborted with 0 of 14,231 records written, leaving the NAVs from 2026-10-12 active. No retries were executed by job-scheduler, causing portfolio-service to serve 2026-10-12 mutual fund valuations throughout the morning.
report.rootCauseStatement: During the scheduled nightly nav-import job at 18:00 UTC (23:30 IST) on 2026-10-13, market-data-service crashed during parsing at line 8982 of AMFI's NAVAll.txt due to an unhandled 'N.A.' value for scheme code 118191. The service aborted the entire import transaction with 0 NAVs written, leaving 2026-10-12 NAVs active. Because job-scheduler did not configure or trigger retries upon failure, mutual fund NAVs remained stale into the morning trading session.

hypotheses.cause: During the scheduled nav-import run at 18:00 UTC (23:30 IST), market-data-service encountered an unhandled parse error on line 8982 of AMFI's NAVAll.txt due to an invalid NAV value 'N.A.' for scheme code 118191, aborting the entire import with 0 NAVs written and leaving stale 2026-10-12 NAVs active without subsequent retries.
hypotheses.rationale: Direct log and metric evidence shows job-scheduler launched nav-import run_7fadae4b at 18:00:00Z. At 18:02:00Z, market-data-service threw a parse error on line 8982 ('invalid NAV value N.A. for scheme code 118191') and aborted the import with 0 of 14,231 records written. nav_age_s steadily increased past 34 hours without resetting, and job-scheduler executed no retries.

hypotheses.cause: The upstream AMFI feed published malformed data containing 'N.A.' instead of a numerical NAV value for scheme code 118191, violating the expected feed contract and triggering market-data-service's import failure.
hypotheses.rationale: The downloaded feed file NAVAll.txt contained an unparseable 'N.A.' string for scheme 118191, which acted as the external trigger for market-data-service's parser failure.

hypotheses.cause: Deployment CHG-48221 on portfolio-service at 03:40 UTC (09:10 IST) containing a valuation code refactor introduced a regression in calculating mutual fund portfolio values.
hypotheses.rationale: Although CHG-48221 coincided with user complaint onset at 09:10 IST, portfolio-service was already logging warnings about stale NAVs dated 2026-10-12 at 02:16 UTC under version 7.2.0 before the deployment. In addition, portfolio valuation errors and stock price ages remained completely normal.

facts.statement: job-scheduler triggered scheduled job nav-import run_7fadae4b at 2026-10-13T18:00:00.000Z (23:30 IST), which failed at 2026-10-13T18:06:00.000Z with exit code 1.
market-data-service downloaded NAVAll.txt (1980 KB) from amfi-nav-feed at 18:01:00 UTC but logged a parse error at 18:02:00 UTC on line 8982: invalid NAV value 'N.A.' for scheme code 118191.
market-data-service aborted the import at 18:02:06 UTC with 0 of 14,231 NAVs written, leaving the previous NAV set active.
job-scheduler did not trigger any retries of nav-import between 18:06:01 UTC on 2026-10-13 and 05:00:00 UTC on 2026-10-14.
market-data-service metric nav_age_s steadily increased from 82,440 seconds at 17:00 UTC on 2026-10-13 to 125,460 seconds (~34.8 hours) at 04:55 UTC on 2026-10-14 without any reset.

portfolio-service logged warnings stating 'fund NAV older than 1 trading day for X holdings (nav_date=2026-10-12); showing last available NAV' as early as 02:16:24 UTC on 2026-10-14, well before the 03:40 UTC deployment.
portfolio-service price_age_s for stocks remained healthy and normal at ~2.01 seconds, and cache hit rates were normal between 92% and 95%.

inferences.statement: The user-facing symptom of stale mutual fund values was directly caused by market-data-service serving 2-day-old NAVs from 2026-10-12 due to the overnight import failure, rather than any calculation error or cache failure in portfolio-service.

The coincidence of user complaints with portfolio-service deployment CHG-48221 at 09:10 IST was due to user app-open traffic surging around Indian market open, exposing the pre-existing stale NAVs that had persisted since 23:32 IST the prior night.

assumptions.statement: AMFI's NAV feed occasionally publishes 'N.A.' or placeholder strings for discontinued, new, or suspended mutual fund schemes.
market-data-service lacked record-level exception handling, causing any single line parse failure to roll back the entire NAV file ingestion transaction.
